thread:
sam: quick question for the group: when users save a per-route query today we capture the model id but not the routing policy. should saved queries lock to a specific model version (immutable) or follow the route's active routing policy (dynamic)?

leah: leaning toward lock-by-default with an opt-out. most customers expect reproducible results when they 'save' a query. if we let policies change the returned model, it breaks QA and alerts.

tom: +1 for default lock. idea: add `model_lock: STRONG|WEAK|NONE` to saved-query metadata. STRONG = always use pinned model, WEAK = prefer pinned but allow fallback per routing policy, NONE = follow route policy always.

product-analytics: note: locking affects analytics comparability. If a saved-query is locked to model v1 but route now uses v2, telemetry and cost numbers will diverge. We should store the snapshot id and a tiny digest of the route policy at save time so diffs are explicit.

eng-api: API sketch quick:
```http
POST /api/v1/routes/{route_id}/saved_queries
body: {"name":"weekly-run","query":"...","model_lock":"STRONG"}
Response: {"id":"sq_123","snapshot_id":"snap_2026_07_15_001","status":"estimated"}
```
We store snapshot metadata (model_id, model_perf_version, routing_policy_digest, seq_histogram_digest).

sam: UX asks: when a saved query is opened in the console, show a small banner: "This query is locked to redwood-7b @ v1.2 (saved 2026-07-15). Current route uses redwood-13b." and a CTA: 'Run with route settings' or 'Run as-saved'.

leah: and for rollouts we should provide a compare view: diff snapshots (latency, cost, median seq len) and show the delta + confidence. If rollback is available, show a one-click 're-lock to latest route model' or 'recompute snapshot'.

product-analytics: we must flag low-confidence diffs when telemetry sample rate < 5% or when snapshot is older than X days. Confidence label affects whether we auto-notify stakeholders on rollout.

eng-api: implementation notes: snapshot creation should be cheap. On save we take cache-based summary + route telemetry histogram. Mark snapshot `estimated:true`. Kick off async job to run perf profiler if needed and update snapshot and confidence score. Snapshots indexed by id so diffs are fast.

sam: question: what about quota ties? if the saved query is locked to a cheap model but route is on tiered quota, we could mislead usage planning. Should snapshot include a `quota_context` field (current plan, dedicated pool id, fallback policy)?

leah: yes include `quota_context` with human readable note: e.g., "hosted: shared-pool-us-west, fallback: redwood-7b when qps>200". UI shows a small risk badge if mismatch.

eng-api: security note: for private deployments, snapshots must respect VPC-only model visibility. i.e., customers shouldn't be able to save or lock to models not available in their tenancy. We'll validate on save.

ops-bot: deployment: saved-query snapshot API changes deployed to staging behind feature flag `sq_model_lock` (v0.9). Endpoints: POST /routes/{id}/saved_queries, GET /routes/{id}/saved_queries/{sq_id}/snapshot

product-analytics: for alerts: propose default guardrails: alert if cost delta > 20% or latency p95 delta > 25% after rollout, only if confidence >= MEDIUM.

sam: next steps: eng-api finalize model_lock enum and snapshot schema, product-analytics to propose alert thresholds, UX to mock banner + compare view. We'll iterate ADR next week.

leah: I'll draft the UX copy for the banner and the risk badges.

sam: thanks all :white_check_mark: "
